_comment: Hand-kept content. Everything else on the site is fetched by build.js from six keyless sources and written to data/site.json. Facts here were verified 2026-08-08 against Wikipedia, Billboard, Korea Herald and Korea Times. This is a live subject — re-check before trusting anything dated.
_siteUrlNote: Drives the sitemap, canonical tag and og:url. Lowercased on purpose — Pages serves from a lowercased host regardless of how the username is cased, so a capitalised value here would point at a subtly different address than the real one. Change this if a custom domain is ever added, then rebuild.
_positionsNote: Positions are fandom convention, not an SM designation — Wikipedia does not list them and SM does not publish them. Taken from the consistent reading across kprofiles, kpopping and the NCT wiki. Each card shows one short primary label because the chip is small; the fuller sets are Taeyong (leader, main rapper, main dancer), Johnny (lead rapper, lead dancer, sub vocal), Yuta (lead dancer, sub vocal, sub rapper), Doyoung (main vocal), Jaehyun (main vocal, lead dancer, sub rapper), Jungwoo (lead vocal, lead dancer), Haechan (main vocal, lead dancer, maknae). An earlier version of this file had every member except Taeyong as 'Vocal', which was simply wrong — Taeyong and Johnny are rappers.
_membersNote: The roster is curated on purpose. build.js parses the Wikipedia infobox every run and reports any divergence in the build log and in site.json's lineupDrift, but it never rewrites this list — an infobox edit, vandalism or a parse regression would otherwise silently rewrite the page. Everything a card shows (Korean name, position, birthplace, status) is curated because none of it is reliably machine-readable. Status is Active or Service; military service is not machine-readable at all.
_lineupLogNote: Membership changes, newest first. Kept factual and dated — the log states that a departure happened and when, and does not characterise the circumstances. Tags: Debut, Joined, Left, Service.

_dropNote: The album the countdown counts toward. `fingerprint` is matched against the live catalogue by build.js, so the moment the release appears in Apple Music or Deezer its real cover art and metadata replace whatever is here. Set `date` in ISO 8601 with the offset — KST is +09:00. Remove this whole key once the countdown is no longer wanted.

timeline.title: Debut
timeline.body: Introduced as NCT's first fixed sub-unit, named for the longitude of Seoul. The debut EP NCT #127 arrived the same week.

timeline.title: Limitless
timeline.body: Johnny and Doyoung joined for the second EP, taking the lineup to nine.

timeline.title: Cherry Bomb
timeline.body: The EP that fixed the group's sound in most people's heads, and still the one fans point newcomers to first.

timeline.title: Regular-Irregular
timeline.body: The first full-length album. Jungwoo joined for it, and Regular charted the group on the Billboard 200 for the first time.

timeline.title: Superhuman
timeline.body: The repackage of NCT #127 We Are Superhuman, and the group's first number-one on a Billboard album chart.

timeline.title: Neo Zone
timeline.body: Second album, and the record that made the neon-green Neo Zone palette the group's visual signature.

timeline.title: Sticker
timeline.body: Third album. Over two million copies sold, and the first NCT 127 record to pass that mark.

timeline.title: 2 Baddies
timeline.body: Fourth album, and a top-three debut on the Billboard 200.

timeline.title: Fact Check
timeline.body: Fifth album, released alongside the group's largest tour to date.

timeline.title: WALK
timeline.body: Sixth album, and the last full-length before a two-year gap.

timeline.title: BLINGY
timeline.body: Seventh album, nine tracks, released for the tenth anniversary as a seven-member group.

timeline.title: NEO CITY — THE REDLINE
timeline.body: Fifth tour opens with three nights at KSPO Dome in Seoul before heading across Asia.

facts: The 127 is the longitude of Seoul. Every NCT sub-unit is named for a city, and 127 is the one that stayed.
NCT was designed with no fixed member limit and no fixed lineup — 127 was the first unit given a permanent roster.
Cherry Bomb is the song most fans name when asked where to start, and it was never even a title track on a full album.
Regular was released in Korean, English and Spanish versions, which is how the group first charted in the United States.
Neo Zone's green is close enough to a signature that fans identify the era from a single frame of colour.
Johnny grew up in Chicago and trained for nine years before debuting — one of the longest trainee periods in the company.
Yuta is from Osaka and joined SM after being scouted at a casting audition in Japan.
The group's fandom name, NCTzen, is a pun on citizen, which fits a group named after map coordinates.
Sticker sold over two million copies, making it the first NCT 127 album to do so.
BLINGY is the group's first full album in two years and lands almost exactly ten years after the debut EP.
